summary: Do not ship this walking skeleton yet. Three load-bearing seams contradict the remaining increments and would institutionalize false-green results or force later redesign.
triage: review-gate SKILL.md § Triage governs: render EVERY finding as a full table row, never inside a dialog; then ask the ROUND before the rows — take every Proposed decision as it stands, or decide row by row — and `as proposed` ends the round in that ONE action; only if row-by-row was chosen, ask per finding with that row's Proposed decision as the first option, a reject or defer taking a free-text reason; echo back ONLY the rows that carried free text, and none if the round was decided by selection alone; max 2 rounds, append decisions.md and COMMIT it with this artifact.

findings.title: Runner invents verdicts instead of honoring the gate result seam
findings.body: `runOne` reduces every child to `{ok, out}`, and `runGates` ignores successful output and synthesizes PASS solely from exit code. A gate that prints FAIL but mistakenly exits 0—or emits no status at all—is reported as PASS. This contradicts ticket 01's output-derived verdict contract and leaves no coherent protocol for planned N/A and BLOCKED results. Adding those states after more gates adopt this boolean seam will require replacing the runner and its public-process tests together.
findings.recommendation: Define a structured terminal gate-result contract now, validate its status token against the exit code, preserve raw diagnostics separately, and add child-process fixtures for missing, contradictory, N/A, and BLOCKED results.

findings.title: Registry/table parity ignores completion semantics
findings.body: The claimed four-place consistency reads the human table as IDs only. Command, `kind`, and N/A policy are duplicated between the table and registry but never compared. Ticket 07 can therefore mark performance advisory in one source and hard in the other while `--check-only` remains green; tickets 09–10 would then copy contradictory completion policy into the harness core and README.
findings.recommendation: Make one typed definition canonical and generate the duplicated table cells from it, or parse and compare command, kind, and N/A columns with negative drift fixtures. Keep only human threshold prose outside the canonical definition.

findings.title: CI parity bypasses the runner-owned artifact DAG
findings.body: Workflow inspection requires literal `bun run <registered-script>` tokens. A single orchestrated `bun run gate --ci` would be rejected as unregistered, forcing CI to invoke gates directly. Once ticket 02 introduces run-unique build directories and artifact-path passing, direct calls bypass that orchestration and cannot satisfy ticket 08's one-build contract without duplicating the DAG in YAML. The raw-text scan also counts commented or disabled commands as executed, permitting false-green CI parity.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit runner CI mode that selects `ci: yes` rows and preserves dependency orchestration. Require the workflow to invoke that entrypoint once, and validate the active YAML step rather than counting raw command text; test commented and disabled steps.

next_steps: Establish the gate-result protocol before implementing ticket 02.
Remove unchecked semantic duplication between the registry and human table.
Redesign CI integration around one registry-driven runner invocation before adding artifact-consuming gates.
